english: Let $\alpha<\beta<\gamma$ be the roots of the equation $x^{3}-7x+6=0$, and let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&\alpha&\alpha^{2}\\1&\beta&\beta^{2}\\1&\gamma&\gamma^{2}\end{pmatrix}$. Then the sum of all the entries of $\mathrm{adj}(A)$ is
hindi: माना कि $\alpha<\beta<\gamma$ समीकरण $x^{3}-7x+6=0$ के मूल हैं, तथा $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&\alpha&\alpha^{2}\\1&\beta&\beta^{2}\\1&\gamma&\gamma^{2}\end{pmatrix}$ है। तब $\mathrm{adj}(A)$ की सभी प्रविष्टियों का योग है
solution: $R_2\to R_2-R_1$, $R_3\to R_3-R_1$ and take out factors: $\det A=(\beta-\alpha)(\gamma-\alpha)(\gamma-\beta)=4\cdot5\cdot1=20$
So the row sums of $A^{-1}$ are $1,0,0$ and the sum of all entries of $A^{-1}$ is $1$
solution_full: Apply $R_2\to R_2-R_1$, $R_3\to R_3-R_1$: the rows become $(0,\beta-\alpha,\beta^{2}-\alpha^{2})$ and $(0,\gamma-\alpha,\gamma^{2}-\alpha^{2})$. Taking $(\beta-\alpha)$ and $(\gamma-\alpha)$ out of these rows leaves $\begin{vmatrix}1&\beta+\alpha\\1&\gamma+\alpha\end{vmatrix}=\gamma-\beta$.
Multiplying by $A^{-1}$: $A^{-1}(1,1,1)^{T}=e_1$. The left side is the column of row sums of $A^{-1}$, so the row sums of $A^{-1}$ are $1,0,0$.
Hence the sum of all entries of $A^{-1}$ is $1+0+0=1$.
Since $\mathrm{adj}(A)=\det(A)\,A^{-1}=20A^{-1}$, the sum of all entries of $\mathrm{adj}(A)$ is $20$.
(Direct check: the cofactor matrix has entries $30,-5,-5;\,-12,8,4;\,2,-3,1$, whose sum is $20$.)
originality_note: New: the sum of the entries of adj(A) for a Vandermonde matrix is obtained without cofactors, from A e1 = (1,1,1)^T, which makes the entries of A^{-1} add up to 1 (way 4, hidden invariant). Closest known: the Vandermonde determinant (beta-alpha)(gamma-alpha)(gamma-beta). Different because: the question is about adj(A) and the shortcut uses the inverse acting on the all-ones vector.

concept_use.Adjoint of a square matrix: adj(A) = det(A) A^{-1}, so the sum of entries of adj(A) is 20 times that of A^{-1}.
concept_use.Inverse of a square matrix: A e1 = (1,1,1)^T gives A^{-1}(1,1,1)^T = e1, so the entries of A^{-1} add up to 1.
concept_use.Application of properties of determinant: Row operations and factor extraction give the Vandermonde value det A = (beta-alpha)(gamma-alpha)(gamma-beta) = 20.

stem_review: Read as a student: every matrix and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked: sympy gives det A = 20, sum of entries of A^{-1} = 1 and of adj(A) = 20 with the roots ordered -3 < 1 < 2; the order is stated so the sign of det A is fixed. Changed: added the order alpha < beta < gamma.
key_step: Seeing that the first column of A is all ones, so the entries of A^{-1} sum to 1, combined with the Vandermonde determinant 20.
justification: Three linked results (Vandermonde factorisation, inverse acting on (1,1,1)^T, adj = det x inverse); the shortcut is not standard, though nine cofactors also work with options to check. Similar demand to the inverse and null-space statements of 2023-P2-Q5 (L3).
